title: League politics searches for a stronger constitutional line
detail: After uneven electoral results in the Muslim-majority provinces and amid wartime political strain, Muslim League leaders intensified debate over how to secure Muslim political power in British India.

title: All-India Muslim League meets in Lahore
detail: The League convened its annual session in Lahore to redefine its political strategy in the context of war, constitutional deadlock, and competing claims about representation.

title: A. K. Fazlul Huq moves the resolution
detail: Bengal's premier A. K. Fazlul Huq formally moved the Lahore Resolution, linking Bengal directly to one of the most consequential constitutional declarations of late colonial South Asia.

title: The resolution is adopted
detail: The League adopted language calling for Muslim-majority regions in the northwestern and eastern zones to form 'independent states' whose constituent units would be autonomous and sovereign.

title: From ambiguous formula to mass political demand
detail: Although the text did not explicitly name Pakistan, the resolution quickly became a central slogan of Muslim League politics and reshaped Bengal's place in partition-era constitutional struggle.
